$comment: PHASE A — D2a EXPERIMENT. Written AFTER requirement.md, by decomposing that prose into these fields, to test whether the production direction (analysis.json -> rendered md) is viable. Friction points are recorded in $comment_d2a keys throughout. Verdict is in coverageAssessment.d2aFindings at the bottom.

purpose.statement: The editing screen for a blog post, serving both creation and modification through one form. It presents a post's title, body, publication date, owning blog, and tags; validates that the first four are provided; and saves the result — creating a new post or updating an existing one depending on whether it already has an identifier.

responsibilities.statement: Present an editable form for a post, populated from the supplied post when one exists.
Offer the available blogs and tags as selectable options.
Enforce that title, body, and date are provided before saving is permitted.
Create or update the post on submission, choosing by whether an identifier is present.
Return the person to where they came from once saving succeeds.

purpose.$comment_d2a: Clean mapping. The second paragraph of requirement.md §1 ('the post is handed to the screen already loaded... it does fetch the choices itself') had NO home — it is a scoping remark, neither purpose nor responsibility. Rendered output would lose it. Suggests a `context` or `notes` string on purpose.

external.name: post being edited
external.description: Supplied through routing data, meaning something upstream loaded it before this screen appeared. This screen never fetches it.

stateModel.$comment_d2a_props: Legitimately empty — no @Input/@Output. But requirement.md said something meaningful here: 'None. Its input arrives through routing instead.' An empty array renders as nothing, losing the explanation of WHY it is empty. Absence needs a voice; a renderer cannot distinguish 'nothing to say' from 'nothing here, and that is the notable part'.

local.description: True while a save is in flight; disables the save control.
The post currently being edited, or nothing for a new one.
The blogs offered in the selector. Despite the name, local to this screen and shared with nothing.
The tags offered in the selector. Also local despite the name.

derived.name: option matching helpers
derived.rule: Two comparison helpers decide whether a selected option matches the stored value, each delegating to the corresponding entity service. Without them the selectors could not pre-select an existing choice, since options are objects rather than simple values.

form.description: Six fields built by a dedicated form service: identifier, title, body, date, blog, tags.
validationRules: Date is required, and defaults to the current moment for a new post.
Blog is optional and may be left empty.
Tags are optional and default to none.
The identifier is marked required and permanently disabled; because disabled fields take no part in validation, its required rule never affects whether the form can be submitted.
Validation messages appear only once a field has been edited or visited — not on arrival.
form.$comment_d2a: MAJOR FRICTION. requirement.md rendered this as a 6-row table (field / required / notes) plus two paragraphs of prose about disabled-field semantics. `validationRules` is a flat string array — it cannot express a table, and the two paragraphs became bullet 6 and 7, losing the emphasis they had as standalone prose. A faithful render of this array would be a bullet list, NOT the table a reviewer found readable. The schema needs a structured `controls` array here (mirroring functions.json#/forms/groups/controls) rather than free strings.

async.trigger: Screen initialization; re-runs on every routing-data emission.
Each routing-data emission, via option loading.
async.errorHandling: None — failure leaves the selector silently empty, indistinguishable from no blogs existing.

async.trigger: Each routing-data emission, via option loading.

async.errorHandling: This screen shows nothing itself; reporting is delegated to an application-wide error display fed by the event bus.

publicContract.$comment_d2a_consumed: Empty, but requirement.md explained: 'Nothing renders this screen directly. Reached by route.' Same absence-needs-a-voice problem as propsAndEvents.

methods.contract: Marks a save in flight, then creates or updates depending on whether an identifier is present. Does not itself check validity — the save control is disabled instead.
preconditions: The form is valid (enforced by the disabled control, not by this method).
postconditions: A create or update request has been issued.
The in-flight flag is set until the request settles.

methods.contract: Returns to the previous entry in browser history.
postconditions: The browser has navigated back one entry.

methods.signature: (a: IBlog | null, b: IBlog | null) => boolean
methods.contract: Whether two blogs are the same, for option matching.

methods.signature: (a: ITag | null, b: ITag | null) => boolean
methods.contract: Whether two tags are the same, for option matching.
UNREACHABLE — never called from template, method, or test.

methods.signature: openFile(base64: string, contentType?: string | null): void
setFileData(event: Event, field: string, isImage: boolean): void

extensionPoints.statement: Four operations exist for subclasses to override. The failure callback is empty by design and carries a comment marking it an extension point.

publicContract.$comment_d2a: `unreachable` and `extensionPoints` are both NOT in the schema — invented here. requirement.md's §4 paragraph explaining WHY the trio is unreachable (generated boilerplate for binary fields Post lacks, two dependencies serving only them) has no field at all; it is a finding about the unit, not about any one member.

workflows.name: Open the screen for editing
preconditions: Routing data supplies a post, or does not.

steps.action: If a post was supplied, populate the form from it and merge its blog and tags into the option lists so the current choices remain displayable.
Fetch available blogs and tags, replacing the option lists when each arrives.

workflows.successOutcome: A form populated with the post's values and selectors offering current choices.

failureOutcomes.result: That selector stays empty, with no message.

workflows.name: Save the post
preconditions: The form is valid — otherwise the control is disabled.

steps.action: Mark a save in flight, disabling the save control.
Read the form's values, including the non-editable identifier.
If an identifier is present, request an update; otherwise request a creation.
On success, return to the previous browser entry.
Either way, clear the in-flight flag.

workflows.successOutcome: The post is persisted and the person is returned to the previous screen.

failureOutcomes.result: The in-flight flag clears so the form is submittable again; this screen displays nothing itself.

steps.action: Return to the previous browser entry, discarding any changes.

lifecycleBehavior.onInitialization: The form is constructed while the screen's fields are being set up, by calling into the form service — creating an ordering requirement that the form service already be available, which the source acknowledges by suppressing a member-order lint rule. Then routing data is watched; each post received is stored, the form populated if present, and selector options loaded.
lifecycleBehavior.onDestroy: Nothing is cleaned up; there is no teardown handler.

orderingConstraints.statement: The form service must be assigned before the form field initializer runs.
Option loading happens inside the routing-data handler, so it re-runs on every emission rather than once.
On success the navigation step runs before the in-flight flag is cleared.

services.purpose: Build the form, populate it from a post, and read it back out.
File handling — used only by unreachable operations.
Broadcast application events — used only by an unreachable operation.

packages.usedFor: Date parsing, formatting, and defaulting a new post's date to now.

externalIntegrations.$comment_d2a: requirement.md §5 carried an explanatory paragraph about the merge-if-absent behavior ('if the post references a blog the fetched list omits, it is added so the selector can still display the current choice'). That is cross-service behavior with no field — it is not a property of any single service entry.

sharedState.state: A broadcast channel other parts of the application listen on.
sharedState.$comment: The sole mutation path is unreachable, so in practice this unit mutates no shared state.

statelessOperations.operation: Create or update a post — request and reply, nothing retained.
Build, populate, and read the form — a pure transformer with no fields.

couplingNotes.statement: The form is constructed during field setup by calling the form service, so that service must be available first.
Save requests do nothing until subscribed to, so the request is issued by this screen rather than by the service call.
Reporting a save failure is delegated entirely to the event-bus-driven error display, so this screen's correct behavior depends on machinery outside it.

serviceLayer.$comment_d2a: The observation that the two locally-held collections are NAMED as though shared but are not had no home here — it belongs to naming, not to the shared-state contract. It landed in §6 prose in requirement.md.

behavioralInvariants.statement: A save must produce an update, not a duplicate, whenever the post already exists.
behavioralInvariants.whyItMatters: The identifier survives to the save call only because the form's raw value is read; reading the ordinary value would drop the disabled identifier and silently convert every edit into a new record.

behavioralInvariants.statement: The save control must remain unavailable while the form is invalid or a save is in flight.
behavioralInvariants.whyItMatters: Validity is not checked inside the save operation, so the disabled control is the only guard against submitting an invalid post or double-submitting.

behavioralInvariants.statement: A post's currently selected blog and tags must remain visible in the selectors even if the fetched option lists omit them.
behavioralInvariants.whyItMatters: Otherwise editing an unrelated field would silently clear an existing relationship.

behavioralInvariants.statement: A failed save must leave the form editable and resubmittable.
behavioralInvariants.whyItMatters: The in-flight flag is cleared on both paths; if it were cleared only on success, one failure would lock the form permanently.

behavioralInvariants.statement: Validation messages must not appear for fields the person has not yet edited or visited.
behavioralInvariants.whyItMatters: A new post opens with required fields blank; showing errors immediately would present the form as broken on arrival.

then: The post's own blog is included even if the fetched list omits it
acceptanceCriteria.coveredByExistingTest: Should call Blog query and add missing value

then: The post's own tags are included even if omitted
acceptanceCriteria.coveredByExistingTest: Should call Tag query and add missing value

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: The form reflects the supplied post
given: A post is supplied through routing
then: The form is populated from it

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Saving an existing post updates it

then: An update is requested, not a creation
acceptanceCriteria.coveredByExistingTest: Should call update service on save for existing entity

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Saving a new post creates it
given: The form holds a post with no identifier
then: A creation is requested, not an update
acceptanceCriteria.coveredByExistingTest: Should call create service on save for new entity

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: A failed save re-enables the form
then: The in-flight flag is cleared so the form can be submitted again
acceptanceCriteria.coveredByExistingTest: Should set isSaving to false on error

given: Two blogs are compared for option selection
then: It defers to the blog service's own comparison
It defers to the tag service's own comparison

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: Saving is blocked while invalid or in flight
given: The form is invalid, or a save is already in flight
when: The person looks at the save control

given: An existing post is being edited and its identifier field is non-editable
then: The identifier is still included, so an update is performed rather than a creation

acceptanceCriteria.scenario: A new post's date is pre-filled
given: The screen opens with no existing post
then: The date is pre-filled with the current moment

given: The screen has just opened with empty required fields
when: The person has not yet edited or visited a field
then: No validation message is shown for it

businessConstraints.statement: A post must have a title, a body, and a date.
A post need not belong to a blog, and need not carry any tags.
A post may carry several tags.
A post's identifier is assigned by the system and never editable.
A new post's date defaults to the moment the form is opened, rather than being left blank.
businessConstraints.$comment: High confidence on the behavior; medium on whether 'the moment the form was opened' is the intended publication semantic.

edgeCases.situation: The blog or tag list cannot be fetched.
edgeCases.currentBehavior: The selectors are silently empty and the person cannot distinguish that from 'none exist'.
This screen shows nothing itself and relies on application-wide error display.

edgeCases.situation: A post references a blog or tag missing from the fetched list.
edgeCases.currentBehavior: The current choice is still displayed rather than appearing absent.

edgeCases.situation: The person wants to express 'no tags'.
edgeCases.currentBehavior: No empty choice is offered, unlike the blog selector; deselecting all entries is possible but not obvious.
Both return to the previous browser entry rather than a known screen, so the destination depends on how the person arrived.

terminology.definition: A blog entry with a title, body, date, an optional owning blog, and optional tags.
The publication a post belongs to; at most one.
A label applied to a post; any number.
Determined solely by whether an identifier is present; there is no separate mode or flag.

migration.$comment: Renders to migration_notes.md. Full prose detail for each entry lives in that file; these are the structured records.

deadCode.statement: Three methods are called from nowhere — not the template, not another method, not the tests. Post has no binary field, so these are generator boilerplate for entity types that do; two dependencies are injected solely to serve them.
deadCode.$comment_d2a: `deadCode` is NOT in the schema. It is the run's highest-value finding and had nowhere to live — not a risk (nothing breaks), not a decomposition suggestion. Strong Phase 0 candidate.

risks.description: The disabled identifier reaches the save call only because the form's raw value is read rather than its ordinary value.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: A form library that omits disabled fields would make every update a creation, silently duplicating records.

risks.description: Save-failure reporting is delegated to an application-wide error display fed by the event bus.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: A faithful port yields an empty error handler and no display, so saves fail in complete silence.

risks.description: Browser history is manipulated directly for both cancel and post-save navigation, bypassing the router.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: Substituting a route navigation is not equivalent — history-back depends on arrival path and can leave the application.
Current failure mode is a silently empty selector; a rewrite may either surface errors (an improvement) or reproduce the defect.

risks.description: Error display is gated on the field having been edited or visited, not on validity alone.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: Getting the timing wrong either nags on arrival or hides problems until submission.

risks.description: The identifier control is both disabled and marked required, making the rule inert.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: A rewrite making the field read-only rather than disabled would suddenly enforce the rule, blocking creation of new posts.

risks.description: The form is built in a field initializer that calls an injected service.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: Building it later or earlier changes whether the form exists at first render; the template dereferences it unguarded.

risks.description: Both option loops identify items by position rather than identity.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: Collections are replaced when loading completes; positional identity reuses the wrong node on reorder.

risks.description: Three subscriptions with no cancellation and no teardown handler.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: Probably nothing — request streams complete and routing streams are believed to be completed on teardown, but this was asserted rather than verified.

risks.description: All six services are application-wide singletons.
risks.behaviorAtRisk: Unobservable for the five stateless ones; load-bearing for the event bus, where a per-component instance would break error display.

suggestedDecomposition.rationale: Form building, population, read-back, date conversion, and defaulting already live in a separate service. That seam exists and should be preserved rather than re-inlined.

Four methods exist as overridable extension points rather than because this component needs them separate; one is an empty body with a comment saying so. Absent an inheritance requirement they collapse into the save call's own handlers.

thirdPartyEquivalence.usedFor: Date parsing, formatting, and defaulting new posts to now
thirdPartyEquivalence.$comment: Behaviorally weighty: decides the wire format and supplies the default timestamp.

openQuestions.question: Should the three file-handling operations and their two dependencies be carried over at all? They are unreachable and appear to be generated boilerplate; porting them reproduces dead code, dropping them assumes nothing outside this screen reaches them.
How is a failed save reported to the person? This screen does nothing and relies on machinery outside this folder, so the actual failure behavior could not be established.
Can the malformed date-and-time message ever appear? The template shows one but the form service declares no such rule.
Is returning to the previous browser entry the intended destination after saving? It is not equivalent to navigating to a known screen and could take the person out of the application.
Should option loading re-run when routing data changes? It is invoked inside the routing-data handler, so it repeats on every emission.
Who listens to the application event bus? Requires a repository-wide index, and bears on the save-failure question.
Do the three uncancelled subscriptions matter? Believed harmless because the streams self-terminate, but asserted rather than verified.

suspectedDefects.description: Option-loading failures are invisible: neither request handles failure, so a person may save a post with no blog simply because the list never arrived.
The identifier's required rule is inert — required and disabled simultaneously, so it can never fire. Harmless today, dangerous if a rewrite enables the field assuming the rule protects it.
The tag selector cannot express 'no tags'; the blog selector has an explicit empty choice and the tag selector does not.

unresolvedReferences: The route definition for this component (outside the folder) — so route path, guards, and the resolver supplying the post could not be identified.
PostService, BlogService, TagService internals — HTTP verbs and URLs are inferred from method names.
The event-bus listener that renders save failures.

coverageAssessment.$comment_evidence: Zero because no ast tier exists to resolve ids against — functions.json and template.json were not produced, so tpl:* and form:* ids in this file are ASSERTED, not verified. In production the referential-integrity checker would fail this file outright. That is the correct behavior and worth noting: Phase A cannot satisfy the evidence invariant even in principle.

d2aFindings.verdict: Viable, but the schema is not ready to render requirement.md faithfully.
d2aFindings.$comment: The experiment: write requirement.md first, then decompose it into this file, and see what does not fit.
worked: Workflows, invariants, acceptance criteria, domain rules, and risks decomposed cleanly with no loss.
Prose stored finished reads the same in either direction — storing sentences rather than notes was the right call.
Structured acceptance criteria are strictly better than prose; a testing agent can consume them directly.
friction: SEVEN fields had to be invented: publicContract.methods[].unreachable, publicContract.extensionPoints, migration.deadCode, migration.isLowerBound, serviceLayer.applicable already existed but sharedState needed a reachability note, plus signature.json's effectivelyUnused / fieldInitializerDoesWork / isArrowFunctionProperty.

stateModel.form.validationRules is a flat string array but requirement.md rendered a 6-row TABLE. A faithful render of the array would produce a bullet list, which reviewers found less readable. Needs a structured controls array.

Empty arrays cannot explain themselves. propsAndEvents and consumedBy are legitimately empty, and requirement.md said something useful about WHY ('input arrives through routing instead'). A renderer sees an empty array and emits nothing, losing the explanation. Absence needs a voice.

Unit-level findings have no home. The paragraph explaining why the dead trio exists is about the unit, not any member — same for the merge-if-absent behavior spanning two services, and the misleading collection naming.
Scoping remarks have no home: 'the post is handed to the screen already loaded; it fetches the option lists itself' is orientation for a reader, not a fact about a field.
d2aFindings.conclusion: D2a's direction is sound — nothing about the prose resisted decomposition in principle. But rendering THIS requirement.md from THIS schema would lose the field table, five explanatory passages, and every 'notably absent' remark. Phase 0 should add the seven missing fields, convert validationRules to a structured controls array, and add a general-purpose `notes`/`context` string to each section so orientation prose and absence-explanations survive.

provenance.$comment: Written by decomposing requirement.md, the REVERSE of production order. Records what the schema must support; does not demonstrate that a renderer works.
